question: Why is difference clearer in the sakala than in akala and higher levels?
premises: Difference appears clearly in the sakala.
The same degree of difference does not appear in akala and similar levels.
The sakala has infinite inner differentiations of similar source-types.
inference: Difference is most explicit in the sakala because its field contains many clearly differentiated source-conditions.
uncertainties: The compound anantāvāntaredṛkṣayonibhedavataḥ is dense and its internal relations are interpretive.
plain_english: Difference is not as clear in the akala and higher levels as it is in the sakala, because in the sakala it appears distinctly through countless inner differentiations of similar source-conditions.
